body: Disk.MakeDir on a backend with real directories (Capabilities.Dirs, DirMaker: local, memory; sftp/ftp/webdav to follow) creates an empty directory that DirExists reports. On object stores (S3, GCS, Azure, ...) it validates the dir, runs as one OpMakeDir (so ReadOnly refuses it everywhere) and writes nothing; DirExists is a list with limit 1, so the directory exists exactly while a key is under it. Rejected: zero-byte 'dir/' marker objects, because a marker is an object that List, DeletePrefix, quotas, mirrors, sync and the records layer would all see and count, other tools reading the bucket take it for a file, and a trailing-slash key cannot survive CleanKey. Callers that need empty directories check Capabilities().Dirs. Local removes a made directory when the last key under it is deleted (the tree mirrors the key space); memory keeps it until DeletePrefix. (2026-10-08, CO-15/CO-16)
title: MakeDir without the Dirs capability is a no-op, never a marker object
